warning_summary: Egypt warned Israeli counterparts roughly three days before Oct. 7 that a major event/escalation could occur.
evidence_update: Rechecked Michael McCaul's post-classified-briefing statement: he said Egypt warned the Israelis three days prior and that a warning was given, while explicitly saying the recipient level was unclear. AP/Times of Israel also preserve an Egyptian intelligence official's claim of repeated warnings about 'something big.' No public primary briefing transcript or named Israeli recipient was recovered in this pass.
gaps: Need Egyptian/Israeli primary record or authoritative inquiry evidence identifying the recipient level and exact content. Do not infer Netanyahu receipt.

warning_source: Foreign ministers of Egypt, France, Germany and Jordan
warning_summary: Official Munich Group declaration warned the deteriorating Israeli-Palestinian/Gaza situation required immediate attention to prevent a major conflagration.
evidence_update: Primary evidence upgraded: German Federal Foreign Office's contemporaneous 11 May 2023 joint declaration explicitly says the conflict needed immediate attention 'to prevent a major conflagration.' This removes content/provenance uncertainty.
gaps: Still need evidence that this warning was directly delivered to a qualifying Israeli government or senior state/security decision-maker; public issuance alone is insufficient.

status: Context / not a separate accepted warning
warning_source: Jordan, Egypt and United States in five-party security process
recipient: Tzachi Hanegbi; Ronen Bar; other Israeli senior political/security officials
warning_summary: Aqaba and Sharm el-Sheikh processes explicitly centered on preventing further violence and de-escalating before Ramadan.
evidence_update: Primary/joint communiques establish that senior Israeli officials participated directly in the five-party process and formally recognized the necessity of de-escalation and prevention of further violence. This is useful evidence of contemporaneous awareness and foreign/regional pressure.
gaps: The communiques are multilateral negotiated commitments, not a clean one-way warning event from a foreign source. Do not publish separately unless minutes/testimony establish a distinct warning delivered by a foreign participant.

recipient: Israeli ambassador in Amman for immediate transmission to Israeli government; named ministerial recipient unresolved
warning_summary: Jordan formally warned that continued violations at Al-Aqsa/Temple Mount would contribute to further escalation and represented a dangerous development that had to stop.
evidence_update: Contemporaneous Jordanian Foreign Ministry material, reported by Jordan Times, states the Israeli ambassador was summoned and handed a protest letter for immediate delivery to his government; the ministry explicitly warned that continued attacks/violations at holy sites could only contribute to further escalation.
gaps: Establish which serving minister/NSC/PMO recipient actually received the transmitted letter and whether the warning should be treated as a distinct strategic-escalation event rather than diplomatic protest.

warning_source: Jordanian Foreign Ministry / Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi
recipient: Israeli ambassador; Tzachi Hanegbi spoke directly with Safadi the same day
warning_summary: Jordan warned that extremist/inciting actions by a serving Israeli minister threatened security and stability and risked further deterioration.
evidence_update: Jordan summoned the Israeli ambassador with a strongly worded protest; contemporaneous reporting says Jordan called the conduct a dangerous escalation threatening security and stability. Separately, Israeli National Security Adviser Tzachi Hanegbi publicly confirmed he spoke with Safadi that evening and issued reassurances.
gaps: Need evidence that Safadi directly conveyed the security-warning substance to Hanegbi or another qualifying recipient, rather than inferring it from the diplomatic sequence. Assess distinctness from broader March de-escalation warnings before publication.
